question: Which order should the tool bar's families take, and does a Recent slot earn a place?
context: The Next tool bar now groups its tools into families (built, flag next-tool-groups, on by default). The order and the recent-tools idea are judgment calls about how the bar should feel, so they are yours. Strips of each option are in the brief.

options.label: Picture first
options.summary: Left to right: Select, Selection, Crop, Measure, then a hairline, then Arrow, Shapes, Highlight, Text, Zoom Callout, then a hairline, then Fill beside its colors. This is what is built and running in Next now.
pros: Reads as what you do to a picture: pick and cut and measure it, draw on it, paint it
Measure sits fourth, two slots from Select, so the redline tool is never far
Fill lands next to the color pair it uses
cons: Arrow, the most used redline tool, is fifth rather than second
Crop sits ahead of every drawing tool even though it is used less
options.mitigation: Every drawing tool keeps its letter (A, L, R, O, H, T, Z), so the bar order only matters when you reach with the mouse.

options.label: Redline first
options.summary: Left to right: Select, Measure, Arrow, Text, Shapes, Highlight, Zoom Callout, then a hairline, then Selection, Crop, Fill. The tools a redline uses lead; pixel editing trails.
pros: Measure and Arrow sit right after Select, where a redliner reaches first
The pixel-editing tools (select a region, crop, fill) read as one family at the end
cons: Breaks the pro-editor convention that selection tools follow the pointer tool
A Photoshop hand will reach for the second slot expecting the marquee and find the ruler
options.mitigation: The families still have hairlines, so the bar still reads as a system, just ordered by how this app is used rather than by Photoshop.

options.label: Photoshop literal
options.summary: Left to right: Select, Selection, Crop, Measure, Fill, then a hairline, then Text, Arrow, Shapes, Highlight, Zoom Callout. Photoshop puts paint before type and shapes, so Fill moves up beside Measure.
pros: Closest to the order a Photoshop user already has in their hands
Type leads the drawing family, as in Photoshop
cons: Fill is split from the color pair it acts on by the whole drawing family
Photoshop has no arrow, highlight or zoom callout, so half the bar is guesswork anyway
options.mitigation: The colors could move to sit right after Fill instead of at the end, at the cost of the zoom control moving too.

options.label: Picture first, plus a Recent slot
options.summary: Option A with one more group at the far end, after a hairline: a clock button that wears the tool you used before this one and lists the last three. Everything else stays where it is.
pros: One click back to whatever you were just doing
Might help when a tool is in the overflow menu on a narrow window
cons: Every tool is already on the bar, and each family button already remembers its last member, so the slot shows a tool that is also somewhere else
It spends 42 points of the width this change just saved
A moving slot is the opposite of the predictability the regrouping is for
options.mitigation: It could appear only when the window is narrow enough that tools have overflowed, so it costs nothing at full width.
